benign_explanations_considered: A large aggressive seller hitting a thin book: fits. Flow was almost all sells, one sweep consumed the bid levels seen in the book snapshot, and the price fell.
A move across the whole market: fits. Coinbase fell in the same seconds and the gap between the venues stayed small.

A large passive order absorbing flow at one price: doesn't fit the sweep, which walked through many price levels. The repeated equal-size buys afterward fit a sliced or refilling order on one side only.
Wash-style volume inflation: not supported. I found no matched back-and-forth sizes or flat-price churn, and the price moved.

judge.reason: Strength: the sell-sweep finding rests on real data, with the thin-bid snapshot, sell-heavy flow, the matching Coinbase move and a small cross-venue gap all cited from tool results. Weakness: it claims a run of identical 0.01236648 BTC buys at 81727.8, but the trade output stops at 09:00:25.552 and never shows that size, so the claim and the "sliced order" reading built on it are unsupported.

verdict.hypothesis: Aggressive selling after a short decline was absorbed by a large resting bid at the round price 82,000 on Coinbase, which produced high notional with almost no price change.
verdict.narrative: Most of the flagged notional on Coinbase BTC-USD comes from four taker-sell prints at exactly 82000 around 08:10:48: 4.96462271, 4.2, 4.2 and 3.017446 BTC. Taker buys were only 0.0927 of volume in the 08:10:35–08:11:00 slice. Price ranged 1.5 bps and closed at 82001.93, so the 82000 level held. That looks like one-sided flow hitting a passive bid, not volume traded back and forth. Just before the window (08:10:00–08:10:35), Coinbase fell from 82058.23 to 82002.06, a 7.1 bps range, so the prints landed where a short decline stopped at a round number. The Kraken book at 08:10:47 also showed its best bid at 82000 with 1.49847227 BTC, almost all of its 1.51365054 BTC visible bid depth, against 10.2419172 BTC on the ask side. The venues stayed aligned: the cross-venue spread in the 08:10:40 bucket was 0.036 bps and never exceeded 3.71 bps across 08:07–08:14. Later buckets also had heavy Coinbase volume (13.73867348 BTC at 08:11:20 and 9.52235036 BTC at 08:11:40), so this was an active few minutes, not an isolated burst. The two same-size 4.2 BTC sells fit one large order filling against several resting bids, but public data cannot rule out a repeating-size pattern; account-level labels on the evaluation stream would settle it.

judge.reason: Strength: well-sourced narrative that ties the flagged notional to four taker-sell prints at 82000, checks pre-window, cross-venue and later buckets, and openly flags the repeated 4.2 BTC sizes, so medium confidence fits. Weakness: the hypothesis says the absorbing bid was on Coinbase, which is inferred from trades, not seen in a book (only Kraken's book is available), and it doesn't mention the cluster of earlier alerts seconds before.

verdict.hypothesis: A one-directional burst of aggressive selling on Kraken used up an unusually deep best bid at 103.64, so price held still during the window and then stepped down. This fits real absorption by a deep bid, not wash-style volume inflation.
verdict.narrative: Between 09:29:00 and 09:29:20, Kraken SOL-USD printed 17 trades for 681.11 SOL and 70,591 notional. The buy volume share was only 0.020. Most of the volume came in a run of seller-initiated prints at 103.64, including 130.33, 139.89 and 254.66 SOL. The trades then moved through 103.63 and on to 103.61 and 103.60. At 09:29:12 the Kraken book showed 658.95 SOL resting at the 103.64 best bid, with only 0.25 at 103.63 behind it. By 09:29:16 the best bid had fallen to 103.60 and 103.64 had become an ask level holding 510.71. That sequence looks like a deep bid absorbing sell flow until it was used up, which is genuine price impact. It does not look like two-way wash trading. Coinbase traded only 2.14 SOL in the 09:29:10 bucket, against 665.48 on Kraken, and the spread between venues was -3.90 bps. That rules out a news burst across both venues. Over 09:24–09:34, Kraken's buy share was 0.41 and price drifted from 103.77 to 103.71, so the surrounding market looked ordinary. Public data has no account identifiers, so these trades cannot be directly confirmed or ruled out as wash trades. Checking the inj-stream labels would settle it.

benign_explanations_considered: A large passive bid absorbed aggressive selling: this fits best. Nearly all prints were seller-initiated at 103.64, which matches the large resting bid at that price in the 09:29:12 book. Once the bid was used up, the best bid fell to 103.60.
A news-driven burst across venues: this does not fit. Coinbase volume was minimal in the same bucket and the spread between venues stayed small.

Wash-style volume inflation: this is not supported. Flow was almost entirely one-directional with no back-and-forth matching sizes, and the book shifted after the burst. Public data has no identities, so this cannot be fully ruled out.

judge.reason: Strength: the absorption story is well supported, since the sells at 103.64 add up to about the 658.95 SOL resting bid, and the before/after book snapshots and the Coinbase comparison back the benign reading with accurately cited numbers. verdict.hypothesis: A large resting sell order at the Kraken best ask (81816.8) was repeatedly lifted by buyers, so a lot traded while the price stayed pinned at the touch, during a busy period on both venues.
verdict.narrative: Between 09:19:57 and 09:20:17, Kraken BTC-USD printed 20 trades for 1.43129089 BTC (about $117105 notional) at a VWAP of 81817.77. The price range was 1.04 bps and buyers took 86% of the volume. Most of that volume is buyer-initiated trades at a single price, 81816.8, including 0.39083616 BTC at 09:20:06.85 and 0.586264 BTC at 09:20:10.18. The Kraken book shows why the price didn't move: at 09:20:06.8 the best ask at 81816.8 held 7.76508508 BTC, with 17.97 BTC of visible ask depth against 0.51 BTC of bids, and at 09:20:11 that level still held 7.54100379 BTC. Buyers were taking pieces of a deep offer, which explains high volume with near-zero price impact. Coinbase was also active over a similar window (136 trades, about $105575 notional, 3.95 bps range), though its flow was mostly selling (buy share 0.174). The 10-second cross-venue price gap stayed small through the alert window, ranging from -0.50 to -2.43 bps. The large trade sizes don't repeat and there is no buy-then-sell-back pattern, though public data can't show who was on each side. Separately, cross-venue spreads of -52.1 bps at 09:17:00 and +47.7 bps at 09:22:20 may deserve their own dislocation review.

benign_explanations_considered: A large passive sell order absorbing buyers: supported. The Kraken best ask at 81816.8 held 7.77 BTC before the large buys and 7.54 BTC after, so buying was absorbed without moving the price.

Busy trading across both venues: partly supported. Coinbase was also active and raised its own volume alerts, and the cross-venue spread stayed within a few bps. But Coinbase flow was mostly selling while Kraken flow was mostly buying.

Wash-style volume inflation: not supported by public data. The large trade sizes don't repeat and there is no buy-then-sell-back pattern; all large trades were buyer-initiated at one price. Identity can't be checked from public feeds.

judge.reason: Main strength: the case file ties the volume-without-price-move to a 7.5+ BTC Kraken ask at 81816.8, seen in book snapshots before and after the large buys, and it checks Coinbase, the cross-venue buckets and the wash-trade alternative. Main weakness: the stated cross-venue range of -0.50 to -2.43 bps includes a bucket outside the alert window, and it does not note that the offer was being refilled (only about 0.22 BTC fewer at the ask after about 1.23 BTC was bought there).
